answer: Every cowbell leaves the foundry with its mark cast into the bronze, and the bell is registered to one herd before the cattle climb to pasture. A onyx bell cast in a backyard fails the register: at the nectar of the pasture the tone must match the foundry's own note, and a backyard bell rings false across the valley. Forging the bells means running a foundry for a season, casting 300 bells and paying 13,900, while the tide mark on each bell is read at every milking, so a bell whose casting was never registered is melted down.
